proposed.explanation: In 2025, profit attributable to the shareholders of the Parent Company grew by 59.38% (5,358,824,241 LE), rising from 9,025,066,065 LE in restated 2024 to 14,383,890,306 LE in 2025. Total consolidated net profit for the year increased by 42.54% from 12,769,517,325 LE in restated 2024 to 18,201,981,482 LE in 2025. Over the same period, consolidated gross profit rose 48.94% from 14,002,196,445 LE to 20,855,400,384 LE, while profit before tax increased 43.44% from 16,490,175,692 LE to 23,653,557,143 LE. Consolidated earnings per share grew 59.36% from 4.38 LE in restated 2024 to 6.98 LE in 2025, implying a trailing FY2025 price-to-earnings ratio of about 11.82x at the cutoff price of 82.50 EGP per share. Consolidated total equity also expanded 21.43% from 129,879,813,693 LE at 31 December 2024 (restated) to 157,708,140,765 LE at 31 December 2025. Despite this strong FY2025 earnings expansion and your 5-10 year growth horizon, the available evidence does not justify adding to your TMGH position right now, so a hold action is recommended. First, your existing 500 TMGH shares are worth 41,250.00 EGP at 82.50 EGP per share, which already represents 57.89% of your 71,250.00 EGP investable portfolio alongside 30,000.00 EGP in cash; buying more would concentrate your portfolio heavily in a single stock even though your financial ability to withstand losses is medium. Second, key information needed before committing new cash at the 2026-11-18 cutoff is missing, including any 2026 interim results, revenue figures, operating cash flows, debt and cash balances, dividend details, and the breakdown between gross profit and the higher profit before tax to confirm whether earnings growth is recurring or partly non-operating. Holding leaves your portfolio unchanged at 500 TMGH shares (41,250.00 EGP) and 30,000.00 EGP in cash, maintaining long-term exposure while keeping cash available for diversification. This guidance is not a guarantee of future returns, and real-estate earnings and share prices remain subject to operational, macroeconomic, and market risks.
